_doc: Degradation of clean DFL tracking toward Metrica automatic tracking. Each value is either a published fact (DATA.md/CHALLENGE.md) or a stated assumption; nothing is fitted to the target data or GT.
_ball_missing_frac: FACT DATA.md: ball present on 59.3% of graded frames (94,214/158,857) -> 0.407 missing. Base hazard is solved per sequence by bisection to hit it.
_ball_gap_mean_s: ASSUMPTION: DATA.md says missing 'in bursts' due to occlusions, crowded boxes, balls in the air; no length published. 1.5 s ~ duration of a duel/aerial ball.
_ball_bias: FACT (qualitative) DATA.md: 'occlusions, crowded boxes and balls in the air all lose it ... disproportionately on the frames that matter'. ASSUMED strengths: hazard x1.35 per player within 3 m (cap 6 -> x6), x4 if z>2 m, x2 if speed>20 m/s.
_drop_ball_z: FACT DATA.md/starter baseline: ATD ball rows are x,y,speed only; no height.
_player_missing_frac: FACT DATA.md: mean 20.5 tracked objects over graded frames for 22 players -> 1-20.5/22 = 0.068 (duplicates below add back ~0.01 object).
_player_gap_mean_s: ASSUMPTION: occlusion gaps ~2 s; no number published.
_slots_per_team: FACT DATA.md: 46 track slots for the match, each slot belongs to one team -> 23 per team. Tracklets get a random free slot (no identities).
_swap: FACT (qualitative) DATA.md: slots 'swap identity'. ASSUMPTION: when two same-team players come within 1 m, their continuations exchange slots with prob 0.3.
_dup: FACT (qualitative) DATA.md: count 'occasionally exceeds 22 when the tracker duplicates someone'. ASSUMPTION: 0.5 duplicate tracklets per team-minute, 0.5-3 s, offset N(0,0.7 m).
_jitter: ASSUMPTION: automatic tracking noise, none published; AR(1) rho 0.9 (smooth, not white, so velocities stay plausible), sigma 0.2 m players, 0.3 m ball.
_ball_dead_mult: ASSUMPTION: achieved ball-missing-rate ratio on dead-ball frames (y==D) vs alive play, solved by bisection (a hazard multiplier gets diluted because dead stretches have few players near a still ball). Docs give no split; base 1.0 = no dependence. Profiles randomise it 0.8-2x so models cannot lean on 'ball missing => dead' or its opposite. Achieved missing ratio dead/alive is logged per sequence.
_false_ball: FACT (qualitative): automatic ball detection, no human correction (DATA.md) -> spurious detections exist. ASSUMPTION: rate per minute, 1-6 frame bursts, half near a visible player (head/shoe), half anywhere on the pitch. Base 0 = off.
_wrong_team: ASSUMPTION: team assignment of tracklets is automatic (no identities, DATA.md) -> rarely a tracklet lands in the other team's slots. Probability per tracklet. Base 0 = off.
_profiles: Cached training/eval degradations (~/mtah-external/cache_deg/<profile>/<seed>/). FACT params (ball_missing_frac, player_missing_frac, slots_per_team, drop_ball_z) are fixed per profile; every ASSUMPTION param in 'randomize' is drawn uniformly per sequence from [lo, hi] and saved in the sidecar JSON. Ranges bracket the base default; none fitted to target data.

nominal._doc: Documented target facts (59.3% ball observed, 20.5 objects) with a spread of assumption values around the defaults.

harsh._doc: Stress profile (captain decision): ball observed ~50%, more fragmentation (more missing, shorter tracklets, more swaps), more jitter and tracker errors. Robustness check, not a claim about the target.

stoppage._doc: Captain decision 2026-11-17. Ball lost much more in dead-ball stretches than in alive play: achieved dead/alive missing ratio drawn LOG-UNIFORM 2-10x, overall missing still the FACT 40.7% (so alive missing falls to ~8-28%), and dead-ball gaps long (mean 10-40 s, i.e. most of a stoppage; DFL dead runs average ~25 s). Justification is documentation only: starter/baseline.py says leaving ball-less frames as D 'is what makes the D class mean anything at all', and the published baseline macroF1 (0.64-0.68) is unreachable unless the tracker loses the ball in stoppages (docs/proxy_check.md: DFL nominal gives 0.36-0.41). No target measurement. Everything else as nominal.

gapstress._doc: STRESS TEST, not a documented-facts profile (captain 2026-11-17): the tracker loses the ball in stoppages AND alive play has more and longer gaps (alive missing 25-40%, gap mean 3-5 s, geometric tail beyond 10 s). Overall missing is ABOVE the documented 40.7% by design. Built for the Metrica games only (their clean data already lacks the ball in ~98% of dead frames; alive dropout added on top). Question it answers: does a model/decoder call long alive-play ball gaps 'dead'?

nominal_lj._doc: Low-jitter variant (captain decision 2026-11-17, external evidence): player and ball jitter drawn LOG-UNIFORM 0.005-0.05 m (near-clean). Reason: clean DFL tracking has 1.5-7% of player object-frames in 5 s stretches spanning < 0.2 m (players standing; degrade.still_share), every jittered profile has 0.00%, so the old jitter range erased a property of real tracking in the external source data. Everything else identical to the base profile.
